title: WoW's Gate That Needed 400,000 Bandages to Open
hook: In 2006 every WoW server had to farm 90,000 copper bars and 400,000 bandages before one player could ring a gong. Then the servers fell over. Were you online when the gates opened?
script: Did you know opening one gate in World of Warcraft took months of farming and then broke the servers? In January 2006, patch 1.9 added the Gates of Ahn'Qiraj, sealed behind a server wide war effort. Both factions had to hand in supplies before the gates could open. The shared list alone asked for 90,000 copper bars and 400,000 runecloth bandages. The Alliance also needed 800,000 linen bandages, and the Horde needed 96,000 peacebloom. At the same time, one player per faction chased a huge quest chain for the Scepter of the Shifting Sands. Whoever finished it got to ring the gong and start a ten hour war across Silithus. Scepter holders who rang the gong during that window earned a black qiraji mount that can never be obtained again. The first server to open its gates was Medivh, on January 23, 2006. Then the trouble started. Players reported hour long login queues, brutal lag and server crashes as thousands piled into one zone. Years later Blizzard admitted the turnout was beyond its wildest imaginings and that it was not prepared. When WoW Classic replayed the event in 2020, Blizzard capped Silithus at around 1,500 players per server. Were you there when the gong rang? Follow for more gaming history.
